correctness.rationale: For C_m: x^m y+y^m z+z^m x=0 (m>=2), N=m²-m+1, the torus coordinates u=y/x, s=u^(m-1)z/x yield 1+s+s^m u^-N=0; since gcd(m,N)=1, its valuation m/N at s=0 forces degree-N function-field extension even in inseparable characteristic, proving geometric integrality. The three coordinate vertices are smooth. When p∤N, f_u is invertible and the torus is smooth. For p|N, p odd and m,m-1 nonzero mod p, f_s=0 forces s0=-m/(m-1), while the residual equation u^N=constant has exactly h=N/p^a distinct roots. At each, w=u^-h is a formal local coordinate; Frobenius converts to Y^q+s^-mφ(s), q=p^a. φ(s) has an exact double zero with invertible second derivative, yielding analytical coordinates X²+Y^q (p odd). The cusp has normalization t²,t^q, delta=(q-1)/2, Tjurina length q. Arithmetic genus m(m-1)/2 then gives geometric genus (h-1)/2. Independent integer and finite-field sanity checks across 287 characteristic-degree instances m<=150 validated factor arithmetic, all given exceptional examples and local double-root identities. The all-characteristic proof is analytical, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: Bad reduction and wild inseparable singularities of canonical Klein/Delsarte plane curves are natural arithmetic-geometric invariants. The full parameter theorem explains exceptional characteristics, exact local analytic types, total Jacobian length and normalization genus simultaneously, including p-adic exponents greater than one; it goes well beyond the known isolated char-seven quartic observation.

limitations: Over algebraically closed fields, m>=2, single plane model; no stable model, descent, automorphism groups in characteristic p, or higher-dimensional hypersurfaces.
